title: Three ways to step off the edge
description:
Each of these functions is correct for ordinary inputs and has **undefined behaviour** for an edge case its author never thought about. Find the edge case in each and fix the function so it does what the comment says.

Undefined behaviour does not mean "returns the wrong value". It means the compiler may assume it never happens, so the damage can show up anywhere. Close each gap at its source.
hints: `average` divides by zero when the vector is empty (and also throws its decimals away). `lastChar` computes `0 - 1` on an unsigned size. `midpoint` overflows when `a + b` is larger than an `int` can hold: add half the **distance** to `a` instead.
